title: The Best Way to Track Your U.S. Savings Progress Monthly
description: Moving beyond 'Checking the Balance' to tracking Net Worth and Savings Rate.
content:
Most people measure their financial health by looking at their checking account balance. If it's positive, they feel good. This is a terrible metric. A high checking balance might just mean you forgot to pay the credit card bill or invest your cash. To truly build wealth, you need to track the 'Vital Signs' of your finances: Net Worth, Savings Rate, and Liquid Runway. This guide explains how to set up a monthly 'CFO Meeting' with yourself to track what actually matters.

Key Takeaways

  • Net Worth (The Scoreboard): Assets minus Liabilities. Track this monthly. It tells you if you are getting richer or poorer overall.
  • Savings Rate (The Throttle): The % of gross income you save. This predicts when you can retire. Aim to increase this by 1% every quarter.
  • Liquid Runway (The Safety Net): Cash / Monthly Burn. Knowing you have '4.2 months of runway' is more actionable than knowing you have '$12,000'.
  • Tools: Automated aggregators (Monarch, Empower, Copilot) are superior to spreadsheets because they pull live data, preventing manual entry fatigue.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US financial accounts are fragmented (401k at Fidelity, Checking at Chase, Mortgage at Wells Fargo). Aggregation tools are essential to see the full picture. Security is handled via 'Plaid' or 'MX' tokens, meaning the app has read-only access and cannot move your money.

The Monthly 15-Minute Review

Schedule it: 1st of the month. Coffee in hand.

Metric 1: Change in Net Worth

Did it go up?
Yes: Great. Was it savings or market growth?
No: Why? Market drop? Or did you spend more than you earned?
Goal: Positive trend line over 12 months (ignore monthly noise).

Metric 2: The Savings Rate

Formula: (Investments + Cash Savings + Principal Paydown) / Gross Income.
Benchmark:
- 10%: Treadmill.
- 20%: Good.
- 50%: Financial Freedom fast.

Metric 3: 'Lazy Cash' Audit

Check Checking Account. Is it over your buffer (e.g., $5,000)?
Action: Sweep the excess to investments immediately. Do not let cash rot.

Which Tool to Use?

  1. For Data Nerds (Spreadsheet): Ultimate control. Privacy. Requires manual entry. Good for really feeling the numbers. Use 'Tiller' to automate the feed into Google Sheets.
  2. For High Earners (Monarch Money): Best paid app ($100/yr). Clean UI, good investment tracking, handles crypto and real estate well.
  3. For Debt Focus (YNAB): If you are negative net worth, focus on budgeting, not tracking wealth. YNAB forces you to assign every dollar a job.
  4. For Free (Empower/Credit Karma): Good enough for a quick check, but clunky and filled with ads/sales calls.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I track my car value?

Yes, it is an asset. But depreciate it manually. Lower the value by 1% every month. Don't let the app assume it holds value.

Does Zillow value count?

For Net Worth, yes. For 'Fire Number' (Retirement), no. You can't eat your house. Track 'Liquid Net Worth' (Investments + Cash) separately.

What if I get discouraged?

Focus on the 'Inputs' (Savings Rate), not the 'Outputs' (Net Worth). You control the saving. The market controls the growth. If you saved 20%, you won the month, even if the market dropped 5%.
